## Simple explanation

An artificial neural network (ANN) is a computer model made of connected
computational units. It learns by adjusting connection weights so its
outputs better match examples or a specified objective.

## Technical explanation

A neural network applies a sequence of parameterized transformations to
input data. A common feed-forward network contains an input representation,
one or more hidden layers, and an output layer. Training typically computes
a loss and uses gradient-based optimization to update parameters.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Neural networks underpin many modern systems for language, vision, speech,
and structured prediction. Understanding their layers, parameters, training
data, and evaluation helps engineers select and operate models responsibly.

## How it works

Each layer transforms its input using learned weights and biases, often
followed by a non-linear activation. During training, the model compares
predictions with target signals, computes gradients, and updates parameters
to reduce a loss function.

## Practical example

A small feed-forward network can classify a tabular record by converting
its features through hidden layers and producing scores for each class.
The predicted class is usually selected from the output scores.

## Common misconceptions

- Neural networks are inspired by biological brains but are not literal
  simulations of them.
- A network with more layers or parameters is not automatically better.
- A model's training performance alone does not establish generalization.
